subject: Proposal: Trim Q3 goals & infra runway extension
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Trim Q3 goals & infra runway extension

Team —

Quick mid-quarter readout and proposal so we can lock decisions before QBR prep. High level: we’re behind on two cross-functional OKRs and continuing to invest in lower-return work. I’m proposing a modest re-scope of OKR-2 and a two-week runway extension for infra support to stabilize the pilot with Nimbus Health.

State:
- OKR-1 (Reliability): green, on track after the June cache work.
- OKR-2 (New routing & batching features): amber — implementation complexity + third-party vendor integration pushed timeline 3–4 weeks.
- OKR-3 (Self-serve onboarding): red for adoption metrics; blocked by OKR-2 deliverables.

Proposal (asks):
1) Trim OKR-2: remove two non-essential routing experiments (A/B experiments on model fallback and custom quantization flags) from the Q3 commitment; keep the core batching and KV cache improvements.
2) Approve +2 weeks of infra dedicated runway (1 FTE equivalent in SRE rotation + priority GPU queue) to cover pilot stabilization for Nimbus Health.
3) Fast-track procurement for the vendor onboarding checklist — I’ve flagged procurement@nimbushealth.com below for any contract questions.

Impact: trimming OKR-2 reduces cross-team scope by ~20% but preserves the primary cost/latency wins. The runway extension prevents us from regressing adoption in the pilot and avoids a customer escalator.

Attachments: OKR_trim_proposals.xlsx (proposal with before/after scope and impact estimates).

Next steps: confirm within 24 hours so we can update the QBR pack and notify Nimbus. I’m scheduling a 30-min sync for tomorrow 9am PT to finalize.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Trim Q3 goals & infra runway extension

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear write-up. I support the goal of protecting the pilot, but want to push back on removing the two routing experiments without seeing the quantified tradeoffs. Can you or Marcus share the telemetry that shows those experiments are low ROI this quarter?

Alternative I’d suggest: postpone one experiment (the custom quantization flags) and keep the model-fallback A/B in a limited canary to capture risk signals. That preserves learning while reducing immediate delivery scope.

On the runway ask: I’m sympathetic to +2 weeks but need specifics on what the SRE rotation will cover and what the acceptance criteria are (SLOs to achieve). Without a clear exit criteria we’ll likely get asked to extend again.

Please add a short table with the metrics we’ll track during the runway extension and the stop/go decision thresholds.

— Jonas

Two operational notes from infra/procurement perspective:
1) If we approve +2 weeks of priority GPU queue, that will require a short procurement exception and a formal ticket to capacity planning. I’ve added JIRA-OPS-3421 to track it. Marcus, can you size the GPU-hours?

Thanks — I can push the exception through if we have the SOW and the GPU-hours estimate.

Subject: Re: Proposal: Trim Q3 goals & infra runway extension — Nimbus context

Looping in a bit more customer color from the sales side. Nimbus is in week 3 of the pilot. Their primary concern is consistent inference latency under load; they’ve indicated SLA sensitivity for production. Two items from their side:
- They requested an explicit SLA target for the pilot (p95 < 300ms) and confirmation around data residency (they require US-only).
- Procurement expects a short SoW for the pilot (attached pilot_sow_v1.pdf) that outlines responsibilities.

From a prioritization perspective I’d recommend we focus the trimmed OKR scope on reliability-first items (batching/KV cache) and deprioritize exploratory experiments that only move the needle on cost-per-token. Reliability matters more for conversion right now.

Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Trim Q3 goals & infra runway extension — Decisions and next steps

Thanks everyone for the quick feedback. Summarizing decisions and next steps so the QBR pack can be finalized:

Decisions:
- OKR-2 scope trimmed as follows: we will remove the two experiments (custom quant flags + model-fallback A/B) from Q3 deliverables. We will run a one-week limited canary for the fallback experiment post-Q3 under an extended evaluation plan.
- Approve +2 weeks of infra priority runway (July 20–Aug 3). Acceptance criteria: p95 latency <= 300ms for two consecutive 48-hour windows under pilot load; error rate < 0.5%. If criteria are not met after two weeks, we escalate to a joint task force.
- Vendor onboarding: procurement to proceed with the pilot SoW. Nimbus to confirm US-only residency — procurement@nimbushealth.com, please confirm by EOD Wednesday.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Marcus Lin: provide GPU-hours estimate and SRE rotation plan by EOD Thu (JIRA-OPS-3421).
- Aditya Rao: circulate signed SoW and customer SLA confirmation by Wed EOD. (attachment: pilot_sow_v1.pdf)
- Vanessa Ortiz: update QBR slide deck and submit final OKR language by Friday 17 Jul. (Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/OKR_midpoint_trim_proposals)
- Laura Bennett: submit procurement exception ticket and start capacity planning approval.

Attachments: OKR_trim_proposals.xlsx, pilot_sow_v1.pdf

We’ll cover this in the 9am PT sync and I’ll circulate the updated slides beforehand. If procurement or Nimbus reports a change to residency or SLA expectations, flag immediately.

Thanks — Vanessa
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
